paragraphs.text: Of like argument with the former. The Arabic prefaceth, when Taluth (i.e. Saul) persecuted him. By this and many the like psalms we may see that David did not complain for nothing; and his singular constancy under so many trials may well make us resolve as Jerome did when he had read the Life of holy Hilarion, he rolled up the book and said, Well, Hilarion (David) shall be the champion that I will imitate.
paragraphs.anchor: A Psalm of David

paragraphs.text: Or, in my meditation. To an effectual prayer must concur meditation, invocation, affection, and belief of audience, as here.
paragraphs.anchor: Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer

paragraphs.text: Heb. lives; so usually called for the many faculties, operations, revolutions, commodities of life.
paragraphs.anchor: Preserve my life

paragraphs.text: Or, from the mystery of evil doers, from the Church malignant, that mystery of iniquity. See the contrary, Psa 111:1.
paragraphs.anchor: Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked

paragraphs.text: Heb. from their tumult, their hurricum, their open force, as well as from their secret fraud. Let thy protection equal their projects, who turn every stone to undo me.
paragraphs.anchor: From the insurrection, &c.

paragraphs.text: The tongue in its form resembleth a flaming sword, and being set on fire of hell, it woundeth deeply and dangerously. It is ordinary with David to compare aulicas criminationes cum armis castrensibus, court calumnies with warlike weapons, Psa 5:6; Psa 5:9-10 Psa 11:5-6 Psa 57:4. See there.
paragraphs.anchor: Who whet their tongue like a sword

paragraphs.text: Heb. bend their arrow, that is, as Psa 11:2, "they bend their bow, they make ready their arrow upon the string," &c. See a like phrase Jer 9:3.
paragraphs.anchor: And bend their bows to shoot their arrows

paragraphs.text: Virulent and venomous, quae leviter volant, non leviter violant; for as Medius in Plutarch saith, though the wound they make be haply healed, yet there will be still a scar, ηη ουλη μενει της διαβολης (Plut.). An aspersion, though not fully believed, leaveth behind it a lower estimation of the party than before.
paragraphs.anchor: Even bitter words

paragraphs.text: Innocence and integrity is no target against calumny; but every Zopyrus shall be sure of his Zoilus, who, right or wrong, will shoot him down if he can, Aliquid saltem adhaerebit (Machiavel).
paragraphs.anchor: That they may shoot in secret at the perfect

paragraphs.text: As the hunter when he lieth hidden in a bush; or as when hedges are lined, as they call it, with musketeers, which gall and kill.
paragraphs.anchor: Suddenly do they shoot at him

paragraphs.text: They are not at all touched either with reverence toward God or respect to man, but are utterly debauched, they ride on without reins, &c. There is an elegance in the original that cannot be translated into English.
paragraphs.anchor: And fear not

paragraphs.text: Thus he riseth in his complaint, and showeth how, by the neglect of piety and humanity, they were grown obdurate and obstinate, yea, confident, or rather impudent, in their evil practices.
paragraphs.anchor: They encourage themselves in an evil matter

paragraphs.text: viz. To entangle and entrap me. See Neh 4:11, {See Trapp on "Neh 4:11"}
paragraphs.anchor: They commune of laying snares privily

paragraphs.text: God, who is all eye, shall, but they, having hid God from themselves, think they can likewise hide themselves and their snares from God. But
paragraphs.anchor: They say, Who shall see them?

paragraphs.text: - εχει θεος εκδικον ομμα

Abstrusissima quaeque exquisierunt; they search the devil’s skull for new inventions; who is ready enough to lend them his seven heads to plot and his ten horns to push at good people. How wittily wicked was Saul to destroy David, if he could have done it! See his counsel to the Ziphites, 1Sa 23:22.
paragraphs.anchor: They search out iniquities

paragraphs.text: Heb. a search searched, i.e. They seek out all occasions, they try all tricks, they do all that can be done to undo me. Whereunto he fitly subjoineth this epiphonema by way of exclamation, Adeo intimum viri et cor profundum est, So deep is the inward part and heart of man (for so I read it)! so deep and fathomless, so deceitful, and desperately wicked.
paragraphs.anchor: They accomplish a diligent search

paragraphs.text: He shall overshoot them in their own bow, pay them home in their own coin; he will deal with them lege talionis, for he loveth to retaliate, see Psa 64:4, they shall find that he can handle his arms a fair deal better against them than they did against David.
paragraphs.anchor: But God shall shoot at them, &c.

paragraphs.text: As was Ahab, and the rich fool, Luk 12:16-21, while he sat pruning himself like a bird on a bough, death fetched him off suddenly by his shaft shot at him, and down be came tumbling. See 1Th 5:3.
paragraphs.anchor: With an arrow suddenly

paragraphs.text: According to Pro 12:13 Psa 59:12. {See Trapp on "Pro 12:13"} {See Trapp on "Psa 59:12"}
paragraphs.anchor: So they shall make their own tongue, &c.

paragraphs.text: With horror and astonishment. Heb. They shall wander about in their flight; this is spoken of their favourites and abetters fearing to fall under the like punishment, and being agitated by the furies of their own evil consciences.
paragraphs.anchor: And all that see them shall flee away

paragraphs.text: Seeing such and such banged up in gibbets, as it were, for a terror to others, Poena ad paucos, metus ad omnes.
paragraphs.anchor: And all men shall fear

paragraphs.text: viz. His power and providence, which some doubt till thus powerfully convinced, as Claudian was by the destruction of Ruffinus.
paragraphs.anchor: And shall declare the work of God

paragraphs.text: Abstulit hunc tandem Ruffini poena tumultum,
Absolvitque deos; et non iam ad culmina rerum
Iniustos crevisse queror; tolluntur in altum,
Ut lapsu graviore ruant -
Not myself only, but all the saints shall be comforted, confirmed, and occasioned to make their boast in God with a holy gloriation, Inde arripient sanctae cuiusdam iactantiae argumentum (Beza).
paragraphs.anchor: The righteous shall be glad in the Lord
